captive_summary: The only on-site gas-fired plant at the Ishikari LNG Terminal is Hokkaido Gas's own Ishikari Power Station (12x 7,800 kW gas engines = 93.6 MW, built inside the terminal grounds, commercial operation Oct 2018, expanded Dec 2020). It is Hokkaido Gas's merchant/retail-electricity generation asset (sold as "Hokkaido Gas's electricity" to roughly 300,000 households) that also helps stabilize an adjacent wind farm via a battery system -- it sells power to the grid, it does not power the terminal's own regas/send-out operations. Direction is the reverse of captive: the plant's waste heat flows INTO the terminal for LNG vaporization and road-heating.
